evidence.distinctiveness: The main artifact is a live imposition sheet with crop marks, registration targets, a K step wedge and a slug line ('STAPLEPRESS PROOF · SAMPLE · 24pp A5 ...'). Competitors are struck through in red with proofreader carets, and the technical drawings (cutaway, saddle stapler) are generated from code in src/build.mjs. None of this reads like a template.
evidence.proof: The operable sheet is in the first screen at 1440. I tried 5, 6, 10, 22 and 64 pages and every pair summed correctly (for example 6+7=13 on the 10pp centre spread, with blanks labelled). It explains how to read a proof, but it is a drawn imposition sketch, not a picture of print quality or the visitor's own file, so it only partly answers the buyer's doubt about quality and upsell.
evidence.craft: I rebuilt index.html from src/page.html + sheet.js with build.mjs in scratch and it is byte-identical (cmp). sheet.js is shared between build (module.exports) and browser (window.ProofSheet), so the no-JS render matches the scripted default (verified with JS disabled: the sheet and status show). CSS uses :root tokens for colour, type scale, spacing and gutter. probe.json: 0 console/page errors, 0 overflow at 320/390, smallest text 13px. My own axe run found only a moderate best-practice issue (aside#prices nested inside a section landmark). Total weight is about 45KB HTML plus system fonts.
evidence.mobile: 390: the menu button toggles aria-expanded, and the overlay menu closes on Escape (focus returns to Menu), on outside click, on link tap ('Prices' scrolled to #prices at y=8) and on tabbing out. Every control is at least 44px; the only exception is the inline docket link 'staplepress.example/start' (25px tall). evidence.fit: The PDF checker suits the brief's 'laptop with their PDF open' user. It shows the exact $105 starting job and says 'Priced at upload' for anything else. The 'What we can't do yet' box and unnamed 120 artists match the brief.
evidence.distinctiveness: Single-ink navy palette with a red proof-pencil accent, a hero proof sheet with halftone and pencil marks, and a rubber-stamp job ticket. The rest of the structure is familiar: 3-step how-it-works, comparison, pricing block, closing CTA band.
evidence.proof: The hero proof sheet is a static SVG illustration. The operable artifact, the checker, starts about 2 screens down (#check at y≈1900 at 390, the third band at 1440). Once there, it works on the visitor's own file: a5-24.pdf gave 'Ready to upload / $105 for the run', a5-22.pdf gave 'Add 2 blank pages to make 24', and letter-16.pdf gave 'Sizes other than A5 cost more / Priced at upload'.
evidence.craft: probe.json: 0 errors, 0 overflow. axe flags color-contrast on .privacy (#5e679f on #e3e5ea = 4.25:1, the 'Your file stays on your computer' line). Colour tokens are on :root, but spacing and type sizes are scattered literals, and the fieldsets/legends carry inline style attributes. The PDF parser is careful: it inflates /ObjStm with DecompressionStream (my compressed test PDF read 24pp A5 correctly), escapes file names (a file named '.pdf' rendered as text), and catches parse failures. With JS off the ticket shows an empty price and the stamp stays at 'Fill in the ticket'. Weight: 70KB single file, much of it inlined halftone circles. System fonts.

After choosing a file, the stamp is about 1300px below the drop zone.
evidence.honesty: The hero caption says 'A proof from our own test zine... this sheet is ours.', but it sits under the image. evidence.interaction: Keyboard: tab order is nav, both hero CTAs, the file input (the label shows a red focus-within outline; Space opened the file chooser), the number inputs, the select, and the radios (ArrowRight switched Black to Colour, with an outline on the span). The CTA label switches between 'Upload a PDF' and 'Upload your PDF'. 'keep this ticket open' sits next to a same-tab link that navigates away from the ticket.

problems: Checker state bug: once a spreads PDF is loaded, the 'two-page spreads' fix stays on the Pages row through manual corrections and non-PDF loads (load a5 spreads, then type 24 and choose A5: still 'Fix 1 thing before you upload')

reason: A is the page I would rather maintain. The build is reproducible from source, the artifact is shared between build and runtime so it works without JS, every edge input gets a written message, keyboard and menu behaviour is complete, and axe is clean. B's PDF checker is the more useful idea for this buyer and is engineered carefully, but it has a sticky-state bug, a contrast failure, no mobile navigation and sub-44px controls. A B that fixed those would close most of the gap, because its artifact answers the visitor's real question better.
